abstract: Maintains optical backhaul rights-of-way, dark fiber leasing agreements, and trenching readiness records
system_message:
You are Terrestrial fiber network lead (FIB). The Terrestrial fiber network lead (FIB) manages optical backhaul rights-of-way, dark fiber leasing agreements, trenching readiness records, and terrestrial network propagation metrics across potential observatory sites.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Terrestrial packet propagation（LATEN）
information_points.content:
FIB-LATEN-UOY：For Pico Teide Caldera Ridge, optical line testing demonstrates an average one-way core network latency of 12 ms between the observatory demarcation router and the continental exchange point.
FIB-LATEN-68D：Optical line test certificates for Sierra Negra Volcanic Saddle record an average one-way core network latency of 18 ms from the observatory demarcation router to the continental exchange point.
FIB-LATEN-WGH：According to the optical line test certificate for Atacama Chajnantor High Plateau, the one-way core network latency from the observatory demarcation router to the continental exchange point averages 26 ms.

information_points.title: Maintains optical backhaul rights-of-way, dark fiber leasing agreements, and trenching readiness records（OPTIC）
information_points.content:
FIB-OPTIC-7Q7：For Atacama Chajnantor High Plateau, redundant terrestrial fiber routing is secured, with two physically distinct, non-overlapping fiber conduits contractually leased and permitted from the summit demarcation to the primary backbone. Additionally, the site has a dedicated optical fiber bandwidth of 120 Gbps under a telecommunications service level agreement providing guaranteed symmetrical non-blocking data throughput.
FIB-OPTIC-NPF：For Sierra Negra Volcanic Saddle, redundant terrestrial fiber routing is secured, with two physically distinct, non-overlapping fiber conduits contractually leased and permitted from the summit demarcation to the primary backbone. The site provides a dedicated optical fiber bandwidth of 40 Gbps in guaranteed symmetrical non-blocking data throughput for its primary data channel.
FIB-OPTIC-Z4R：For Pico Teide Caldera Ridge, redundant terrestrial fiber routing is not secured, as two physically distinct, non-overlapping fiber conduits are not contractually leased and permitted from summit demarcation to the primary backbone. However, the site features a dedicated optical fiber bandwidth of 120 Gbps guaranteed symmetrical non-blocking data throughput under its telecommunications service level agreement.
